identity.name: Kingdom of Odoacer
alt_names: Kingdom of the Germanic foederati in Italy

land.text: Italy and the Alpine and Danubian remnant of the Western Roman Empire, taken when 'Odoacer, leader of the Germanic foederati in Italy, captured Ravenna'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria has no row for this kingdom; its 476 Kingdom of Soissons shape holds Dalmatia, and Cliopatria's Ostrogoths row (490-499) draws Italy for Theodoric from 490.

land.text: Italy, where Theodoric 'in 493 founded the Ostrogothic Kingdom'; 'Ostrogothic power was fully established over Italy, Sicily, Dalmatia and the lands to the north of Italy' around 500

successors.note: Cliopatria's Ostrogoths row (455-499) carries Theodoric's Italy from 490 and the Ostrogothic Kingdom row begins 500; eu-06 decides the slug.

capitals.name: Ravenna
capitals.note: 'with Ravenna as his capital'; Theodoric took it on the surrender of 5 March 493 and 'would set up his capital' there.

rulers.name: Odoacer
rulers.title: rex (king), dux and patrician
rulers.note: Infobox '4 September 476 - 15 March 493'; his troops proclaimed him king (rex) on 23 August 476; the Eastern emperor 'conferred upon Odoacer the title of Patrician'; he minted gold in Nepos's name and 'only nominally accepted Nepos's rule' (Nepos page).

correction.text: Italy and the Alpine and Danubian remnant, with Sicily from 476

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 476-480: Italy and the Alpine and Danubian provinces the Western Roman Empire held in 475, plus Sicily ceded by the Vandals in 'September or October 476' (Clover). Dalmatia stays with Julius Nepos until his murder on 9 May 480. The pages give Italy 476-493 as the core and name Noricum only in 487/488; the Alpine and Pannonian extent is read from the 475 Cliopatria shape of the Western Roman Empire (about 0.34 M km2, Italy, Noricum, Raetia, Slovenia). No infobox area on the Odoacer page, so no comparison.

New keyframe for 481-487: Dalmatia added. 'Only in late 481 or 482 did Odoacer invade Dalmatia' after Nepos's murder (9 May 480); the Odoacer page says he annexed it 'within two years' (about 481-482).

correction.text: the 481 shape plus the Rugians' land

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 488-493: 'In 487/488, Odoacer led his army to victory against the Rugians in Noricum'; Cliopatria's Rugiland shape (14,526 km2, north of the Danube) is added. From 489 Theodoric's Ostrogoths contest Italy; the shape is held to 5 March 1493 as the page has Odoacer holding Ravenna until its surrender.

ledger.note: 4 September 476: Odoacer deposes the last Western emperor and rules Italy. 'compelling the young emperor Romulus to abdicate on 4 September'; his troops proclaimed him king (rex) on 23 August 476 after the revolt against Orestes (killed at Placentia). The Senate sent the Western regalia to Zeno, who made him patrician. Infobox reign '4 September 476 - 15 March 493'.

region.text: the Alpine and Danubian provinces (Noricum, Raetia, the Pannonian remnant) held with Italy in 475

ledger.note: 476: the rest of the Western Empire's Italian-Danubian land passes with Italy. The Odoacer page names Italy and, in 487/488, Noricum; the extent is bridged from the 475 shape of the Western Roman Empire (page silent).

region.text: Sicily: 'F. M. Clover dates this cession to September or October 476'

ledger.note: autumn 476: the Vandals cede Sicily. The Odoacer page says the Vandals invaded Sicily in 490, so Odoacer's hold afterwards is unclear; the page gives no tribute terms.

region.text: Dalmatia: Odoacer 'established his own rule in Dalmatia' after Nepos was 'murdered on 9 May 480, at his villa near Salona'

ledger.note: late 481 or 482: Odoacer annexes Dalmatia. 'Only in late 481 or 482 did Odoacer invade Dalmatia' and put Nepos's count Ovida to death; the Odoacer page says he took it 'within two years'; the Western Roman Empire page has 'The murder of Nepos in 480 prompted Odoacer to invade Dalmatia'.

region.text: the Rugians' land in Noricum, north of the Danube

ledger.note: 487/488: Odoacer defeats the Rugians in Noricum. 'In 487/488, Odoacer led his army to victory against the Rugians in Noricum'; the page adds that the Lombards settled the abandoned province by 493. Cliopatria's Rugiland row runs to 489.

region.text: Italy, which Theodoric entered across the Julian Alps

ledger.note: 489: Theodoric's Ostrogoths cross the Julian Alps into Italy. 'In 489, Theodoric led the Ostrogoths across the Julian Alps and into Italy'; the Rugii 'joined the Ostrogoths'. The battles of 489-492 are not on the page read; the whole of Italy is the contested zone.
5 March 493: Ravenna surrenders. 'After the city surrendered on 5 March 493'; Theodoric killed Odoacer ten days later at a meal (15 March 493).

region.text: Italy and the lands held with it, now Theodoric's

ledger.note: 15 March 493: Theodoric kills Odoacer and founds the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy. 'It was also at this time that Odoacer was killed by Theodoric's own hand' (Ostrogoths page: 'in 493 founded the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy after defeating Odoacer'); Odoacer page: 'slain by Theodoric while they shared a meal', infobox 15 March 493.

wars.name: Revolt of the foederati against Orestes
wars.outcome: The foederati proclaimed Odoacer king on 23 August 476, Orestes was killed at Placentia and Romulus Augustulus abdicated on 4 September; Odoacer ruled Italy, with Julius Nepos left in Dalmatia.

wars.name: Odoacer's conquest of Dalmatia
wars.outcome: After Nepos's murder on 9 May 480 Odoacer invaded Dalmatia in late 481 or 482 and annexed it.
wars.note: The Western Roman Empire page implies 480; the Nepos page 'late 481 or 482'.

wars.name: Odoacer against the Rugians
wars.outcome: Odoacer led his army to victory against the Rugians in Noricum in 487/488; the Lombards later settled the abandoned province (by 493).

wars.name: Theodoric's conquest of Italy
wars.outcome: Theodoric crossed the Julian Alps in 489, besieged Odoacer in Ravenna, which surrendered on 5 March 493, and killed him ten days later; the Ostrogothic Kingdom followed.
wars.note: The Ostrogoths page dates the founding of the kingdom to 493; no battle is dated on the pages read.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty borders; Italy is the core and the Alpine and Danubian extent is read from the 475 Cliopatria shape of the Western Roman Empire.

sources.title: Odoacer
sources.note: Reign dates, 23 August and 4 September 476, Orestes, Sicily from the Vandals, Dalmatia 481/482, Noricum 487/488, the war with Theodoric 489-493, the surrender of 5 March 493 and death on 15 March.

sources.title: Julius Nepos
sources.note: Nepos in Dalmatia 475-480 and Odoacer's invasion of Dalmatia in late 481 or 482.

sources.title: Ostrogoths
sources.note: Theodoric's invasion of 489, the capture of Ravenna by 493, the founding of the Ostrogothic Kingdom and the lands held about 500.

sources.title: Western Roman Empire
sources.note: Odoacer captured Ravenna on 4 September 476; the murder of Nepos 'prompted Odoacer to invade Dalmatia'.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks (Kingdom of Soissons known-problems note): slug kingdom-of-odoacer, cliopatria_names [], all three keyframes new. Cliopatria draws Italy 490-499 as part of its Ostrogoths row (1624 cells) and has no Italian polity 476-489 (the Vandal Kingdom shape covers 160 Italian cells, i.e. Sicily and the islands, in 476). The Odoacer page names no boundary and no area; the Alpine and Danubian extent is bridged (event confidence 1). Disagreements: Dalmatia taken 480 (Western Roman Empire page), late 481 or 482 (Nepos page) or about 481-482 (Odoacer page); Sicily 'September or October 476' (Clover) with Vandal tribute not on the page; Odoacer's hold on Sicily after the Vandal invasion of 490 is unclear. The battles of 489-493 (Isonzo, Verona, Adda, siege of Ravenna) are not on the pages read; a gap-filler could open Theodoric the Great or Ostrogothic Kingdom. Wikidata id unknown (null): wikidata.org is unreachable. The family 'italy' is a choice; 'rome' would keep the Western Roman hue. Page budget: no allowance in the brief for this new state; Odoacer and Julius Nepos were opened for the Western Roman Empire dossier, Ostrogoths for the 455 Illyricum cut.
